prompt: Why are attention scores divided by the square root of the key dimension?
options: To make the weights sum to two
To keep the variance of the scores near one, so softmax keeps useful gradients
To remove the need for a mask
To make the output the same size as the input
explanation: The variance of a dot product grows with the dimension. Scaling by the square root keeps softmax out of its saturated regime.

prompt: In a causal language model, which positions may token 2 attend to?
explanation: The causal mask hides future positions, so token 2 sees itself and everything before it.

options: One attention over the full features, repeated h times
Several attentions on separate slices of the features, concatenated and projected
A recurrent update for each head
The average of the token embeddings
explanation: Each head attends on its own subspace, which lets different heads capture different relationships. The results are concatenated and projected back.

prompt: Why do transformers need positional information?
options: Attention is invariant to the order of the tokens, so position must be added
explanation: Permuting the tokens permutes the attention outputs but otherwise leaves them unchanged, so the model has no notion of order unless it is given one.

prompt: A sinusoidal positional encoding gives position 0 the pattern…
explanation: At position zero every sine is zero and every cosine is one, so the even entries are 0 and the odd entries are 1.
